chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) saw a storyteller in the mosque, so he struck him with the whip and expelled him.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Title of Imam Ali)
key_terms.الدِّرَّة: The whip (a small stick or rod used for light corporal punishment)
key_terms.قَاصّ: Storyteller (one who narrates stories, often for entertainment)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali do when he saw a storyteller in the mosque?
ai.summary: This brief narration from *Al-Kafi* illustrates Imam Ali’s (AS) active role in maintaining the sanctity of the mosque by removing storytellers (*Qussas*) whose tales might distract from worship or introduce unverified narratives. The physical act of striking with a *durrat* (a type of cane or whip) signifies a disciplinary measure rather than mere punishment, reflecting the Imam's judicial authority to preserve the spiritual atmosphere of the sacred space. This incident underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on purifying communal spaces from distractions that may dilute religious focus.
